recipes.name: Oven Fried Potatoes II
ingredients_raw: 2 large baking potatoes, cut into wedges

steps.text: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil and spray with vegetable cooking spray.
In a shallow bowl combine oil and lemon juice. Dip potatoes in oil/lemon mixture and season with salt and pepper, to taste. Place on baking sheet.
Bake in preheated oven for 20 minutes. Remove from oven and turn wedges over. Return to oven and continue cooking until crisp and brown on both sides, about 10 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Oven Fried Potatoes II
raw_recipe.description: Potatoes, wedged, rolled in a mixture of lemon juice and oil, and baked in hot oven.

review.reviewBody: I served these potatoes with the chicken fried chicken from this site, and they were delicious! I'm not a big fan of anything lemon, but my mom and grandma were visiting, so I decided to make these because it seemed like something they would like. I ended up loving them, too! I used Morton's Nature Seasoning, and I only had bottled lemon juice, so that's what I used. I was surprised that the lemon really added such a good flavor. These will be a regular at my house!

It is a keeper. Par cooked 2 minutes in the microwave before cutting. Added olive oil, garlic salt, onion powder, and mixed herb seasoning. Cooked 15 minutes as directed, turned for 15 more minutes. Wow.

I cut the potatoes into thin fries and par boiled them for about 4 minutes before tossing with the oil and lemon juice. Added a few shakes of seasoned salt and oregano. Very good. (Even though I boiled the potatoes to give them a head start, I had to bake them much longer - maybe 15 minutes more - to get them as crispy as I like.)

Here are my reasons for 3 stars: 1) raw potatoes are extremely difficult to cut and require more prep time and 2) At the 20 minutes mark when I turned the wedges over they were ALL very soft and I knew the baking time/temp wasn't right. I baked them for 5 minutes more while I heated up vegetable oil in a pan. Then, I fried the fries for about 5 minutes and topped off with some Kosher salt. YUM!

Easy and very tasteful. I did adjust by cooking some bacon and onion to crumble into mixture, a few apple slices and a touch of chili powder. After bakcing, added shredded cheese as topping and broiled to get nice crisp topping.

These were very good!! I did use more lemon juice and used a seasoned salt. I also raised the temp to 450
For the last 10 mins. I wanted them to brown more. Great flavor! Definitely will make them again.

I thought this turned out very well. I mixed up everything "shake n bake" style in a large ziploc bag and it turned out nicely. I added some finely chopped garlic and sprinkled parsley on the potatoes before baking.
Quick, easy and very tasty. I used olive oil and a bit more lemon then called for. I cut the wedges on the thin side, and course cracked the pepper with sea salt.Looked lovely, tasted great!

I used 2 large potatoes for 2 people. Very easy to make and good but imo this recipe needs more kick. I added garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper and it still was just ok. Next time I would add another tbsp of lemon and more of all the seasonings above.

We used potatoes we received from the CSA instead of baking potatoes. Instead of vegetable oil we used canola oil. Also used sea salt and fresh ground pepper. After they were done baking we topped them with fresh grated Parmesan cheese. Tasted really good. We will be making them again.
This is the way I have always made my steak fries. I top them with grated cheese (and melt), crumbled bacon and serve with ranch dressing! YUM! Thank you!
perfect they were delish, I did add a little garlic powder and paprika
Added granulated garlic + fresh-ground pepper; great taste, good texture, yum!
Perfection!!
super yummy - the kiddos loved them! Keep them a little thick or they will crisp up fast.

It was my first time making oven fried potatoes and I love it!!! The lemon juice it did gave it a wonderful flavor. I decided to add dried thyme to add more flavor to it. My kids love it! :-D I will definitely make it again. Besides is healthier than deep fried french fries. Thank you for sharing your recipe Pnylli. God bless...

I tried this and just changed a few things to use what was on hand. I used olive oil cooking spray and olive oil instead of vegetable oil. I also used key lime juice instead of lemon. The potatoes turned out delicious-I was surprised they were so tasty. I plan on making these again soon.
These were okay, but not great. Needs more seasoning.
Yummy! These turned out great! My three year old was a huge fan!

I would definitely recommend using olive oil rather than vegetable oil since in my opinion would be the only thing that would make one want to bake them rather than fry them, to safe the fat content. I also sub'ed the salt and pepper for a no salt seasoning from Costco that has many other herbs and spices in it. The citrus gives it a nice variation.
